extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, publishers, and policy-makers interested in the study and reform of peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative and research-oriented criteria for studying, measuring, and reforming journal-coupled peer review (including open peer review, preprint overlays, and editorial practices). A roadmap for producing rigorous research and standards about peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish peer review studies as a discrete research field
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer Review Studies must be established as a discrete multi-disciplinary and global research field, combining elements of social sciences, history, philosophy, scientometrics, network analysis, psychology, library studies, and journalology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as a foundation for coordinated research programmes and collaborations between researchers and publishers; secure funding and build shared infrastructures to support sustained inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define a minimum standard for what constitutes peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: To reach a global consensus on, and define a minimum standard for, what constitutes peer review; possibly as a 'boundary object' in order to accommodate field-specific variations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create definitional clarity that can accommodate disciplinary differences while supporting comparability across studies and implementations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct a full systematic review of global peer review knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: To conduct a full systematic review of our entire global knowledge pool of peer review, so that the gaps in our knowledge can be more rigorously identified and quantitatively demarcated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use systematic methods to map existing evidence before designing further empirical work; this will reveal where primary research is most needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of editorial conflicts of interest and documenting editorial misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Declaration of editorial conflicts of interests and documenting any editorial misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise measuring and requiring editorial COI disclosure; study prevalence and effects of misconduct and transparency practices on outcomes of peer review and publication decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectations, motivations and competencies of reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations for, and motivations and competencies of, reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify baseline knowledge and skills to form core competencies for reviewers; study what motivates reviewers and what training or recognition would improve review quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researcher attitudes towards elements of open peer review (OPR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Researcher attitudes towards the various elements of [open] peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirically investigate attitudes across disciplines, changes over time, consistency between attitudes and practices, and which OPR systems and features users prefer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design a core outcome set for peer review research
rubrics_metrics.description: Designing a core outcome set would help to optimise and streamline the process to make it more efficient and effective for all relevant stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agree on a set of outcomes (metrics) to be measured in peer review studies to support comparability and meta-research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create joint infrastructure for data sharing and minimal reporting standards
rubrics_metrics.description: A joint infrastructure for data sharing is required as a foundation, based around a minimal set of criteria for standards and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop shared open data repositories and minimal reporting checklists so peer-review research is reproducible and comparable across studies and publishers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value peer review in hiring, promotion and tenure processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review needs to be taken seriously as an activity by hiring, review, promotion and tenure committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise and reward peer-review work to incentivise learning and competence, and consider the effect on early-career researchers and other vulnerable groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish peer review reports and study effects
rubrics_metrics.description: An increasing push to publish review reports (open reports) as a solution to transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate whether publishing reports deters reviewers or changes their behaviour (tone, criticalness, length, submission time), and note that public reports will be skewed toward reviews of ultimately published articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish intrinsic peer-review biases from socio-cultural influences
rubrics_metrics.description: Care needs to be taken to distinguish which biases/traits are intrinsic to peer review itself and which are passively entrained within peer review due to larger socio-cultural factors within research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess and contextualise biases deeply to understand origins and to design mitigation strategies that target the right causal layers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure epistemic diversity and consequences of epistemic exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: It is imperative to understand not only the diversity of opinions that are being excluded in peer review, but also the consequences of epistemic exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify epistemic diversity in reviewer and editor pools, study effects of centralised/ homogeneous communities on excluded perspectives, and link to replicability and innovation outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess peer review's impact on innovation versus conservatism
rubrics_metrics.description: There is relatively little understanding of the impact of peer review on innovation; peer review may lead to conservatism through suppression of innovation or greater acknowledgement of limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate the dynamic trade-off between rapid dissemination/novelty and slow critical assessment/quality control and identify where peer review supports or suppresses breakthrough research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess editorial role in arbitration, quality control, and community engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors play a prominent role in arbitration, quality control, and encouraging engagement while fostering a community environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research how editorial mediation affects review outcomes, engagement in open systems, conflict detection, and overall review quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate open participatory peer review models and editorial mediation removal
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether and to what extent open participatory processes require editorial control, and what impact removing editorial mediation would have on open participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare editorially mediated open models to fully open participatory ones with respect to quality, conflict-of-interest detection, uptake, and sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure uptake and sustainability of preprint-overlay and de-coupled peer review services
rubrics_metrics.description: There are innovative services that decouple peer review from journals (preprint overlays, independent review/recommendation services), but their general uptake appears low.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study motivations for engagement, sustainability, and the downstream fate of articles reviewed via these services (published in journals or not).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess different peer review procedures' ability to flag problematic publications
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability of different peer review procedures to flag problematic publications remains to be evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirically test and compare procedures (traditional, interactive, open, blinded) for their capacity to identify errors, fraud, or other issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure inter-rater reliability of peer review and its determinants
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter-rater reliability and its determinants (how consistent are reviewers) are important to quantify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multilevel meta-analytic approaches to identify factors that increase or decrease reliability across disciplines and journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess effects of blinding and signing on review quality and recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies of single-blind vs double-blind vs open (signed) reviews show variable effects; need to evaluate whether masking or signing improves review quality or changes recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage randomized trials and observational studies cited (e.g., BMJ, JAMA trials) to determine impacts on recommendations, bias, and review quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and standardise roles and tasks of peer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify the roles and tasks of peer reviewers in the manuscript review process (what reviewers are expected to do).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use scoping and systematic reviews to list concrete tasks and responsibilities to inform training, expectations, and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop and evaluate tools to assess the quality of peer review reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Tools used to assess the quality of peer review reports need methodological evaluation and standardisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct methodological systematic reviews of existing tools and create validated instruments for assessing report quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure costs, time, and efficiency of the peer review system
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate human time and financial cost of peer review and the inefficiencies from reject–resubmit cycles (e.g., prior estimates of £1.9 billion per year and 15 million wasted hours).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform cost–benefit analyses comparing quality control benefits to time and monetary costs; quantify redundancy losses and potential efficiency gains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess demographic participation, nepotism, prestige effects and network biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review is affected by demographic and network factors (nepotism, prestige bias, centralised communities) that influence fairness and replicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify how prestige, networks, nationality, gender, and nepotism influence decisions and outcomes; design interventions (blinding, policy changes) accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop metrics and incentives to value reviewers' contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Create ways to value reviewers (e.g., F3-index) and incentivise high quality reviewing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research how formal recognition, metrics, or credit systems affect reviewer behaviour, recruitment, and review quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand motivations and drivers of public commenting and engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: On open commenting systems, user engagement tends to be relatively low for research articles; motivations for who comments and why require study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate incentives, platform design, editorial moderation, and community norms that influence public commenting and persistent engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for skew introduced by publishing only reviews of accepted/published articles
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of public review reports will be inherently skewed based on the articles that are ultimately published and may exclude reviews for articles which remain rejected or ultimately unpublished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analysing published reviews, control for selection bias and seek ways to include reviews of rejected/unpublished manuscripts where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematise vocabulary and standards for comparability across peer review research
rubrics_metrics.description: State-of-the-art research should employ similar vocabulary and standards to enable comparability between results within a cohesive and strategic framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt shared terminologies, reporting guidelines, and core outcomes to facilitate meta-research and cross-study synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess peer review's impact on reproducibility and replicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate how peer review practices affect reproducibility of research and whether peer review improves the replicability of findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link peer review models and behaviours to downstream reproducibility metrics; use reproducibility studies and meta-research as outcome measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine peer review's role as a gatekeeper (assigning imprimatur)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review assigns an imprimatur—a 'stamp of approval'—over which knowledge enters the scholarly record and can thus be built upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study how peer review functions as a gatekeeper of academic capital and trust, and whether it effectively filters for quality or perpetuates inequalities in knowledge circulation.
